records.name: Philadelphia Block Captain Program
records.summary: A city program where one resident per block takes on the job of keeping the block clean and connected: captains organize cleanups and block projects and pass along city news to neighbors.
records.what_you_do: Organize street cleanups, plan block projects like block parties, pass along trash day news, and act as the go-between for neighbors and city offices.

schedule.text: Captains set their own cleanup and block dates. The city holds a yearly captains' rally and a Clean Block Contest.

first_step.how: Call the Philadelphia More Beautiful Committee at 215-685-3971 to find out whether your block has a captain. To start one, ask for the petition: it needs signatures from 51 percent of the block's residents.
first_step.basis: Becoming a captain needs a petition signed by a majority of the block, so the way in is clear but takes organizing with neighbors.

records.notes: About 6,000 captains took part, per a July 2024 article. The city does not publish captains' names, so no names or block lists are recorded here. The newest source is a Jan 6, 2026 city guide. The phone number is from a 2023 article and was not re-checked on a city page.

records.name: Tikkun Olam Coordinating Team at Germantown Jewish Centre
records.summary: A volunteer team at Germantown Jewish Centre that runs community follow-ups on election security and voter protection, including a spring 2026 Zoom session to plan what neighbors could do.
records.what_you_do: Share voter education, learn about poll worker and poll watcher roles, and talk through local actions. Members can bring their own ideas.

schedule.text: A Zoom session on Monday, May 18, 2026, 7 to 8:30 pm. No later date was on the page.

first_step.how: RSVP to the team contact through the synagogue office at 215-844-1507 or office@germantownjewishcentre.org to get the Zoom link for the next session
first_step.basis: The session is open and invites outside ideas, but the way in is an RSVP and the page does not describe a regular schedule

records.notes: The page does not say whether the team itself is nonpartisan, so no claim is made about that. The page links to a few outside groups (ACLU of Pennsylvania, Committee of Seventy, Election Protection, Philadelphia Neighborhood Networks Action Network) that are recorded as leads. The volunteer's personal email on the page was left out; the synagogue office contact is used instead. Only one dated event was found, so the team may be less active than the status suggests.

records.name: League of Women Voters of Philadelphia
records.summary: A voting rights group that works on voter education and registration in Philadelphia. Members staff tables at public events and sign up volunteers for shifts.
records.what_you_do: Staff voter information tables, sign up for election-day and voting-rights events, and join with partner groups on public actions.

schedule.text: Public events are posted as they come up. The most recent one found was a Day of Action on Aug 8, 2026, at Shissler Recreation Center in Fishtown, with tabling shifts for voting rights.

first_step.how: Sign up for an upcoming tabling shift on the event page, or ask the chapter how to join its committees
first_step.basis: Event shifts are posted publicly, but the chapter's membership and meeting process could not be confirmed

records.notes: The chapter's own website was not found. palwv.org/philadelphia returned a 404, and lwvspa.org pages describe a Florida chapter, so they were not used. Nonpartisan status comes from a Philadelphia Citizen guide seen in search results, which was not opened, so it is not stated in the summary. Historical records (1920 to 1984) are held by the Historical Society of Pennsylvania. Verify the chapter website and contact before publishing.

records.name: Fishtown Neighbors Association
records.summary: The neighborhood association for Fishtown. Neighbors meet at general membership meetings, work on beautification, safety and planning committees, and run community events such as a holiday party and a chili cookoff.
records.what_you_do: Attend general meetings, join a committee like Beautification or Safety and Planning, help run neighborhood events, or register voters through the association's voter program.

schedule.text: General membership meetings are held in the evening at the Fishtown Recreation Center. The most recent listing found was Wednesday, Aug 19, 2026, 7 to 8:30 pm. The next date was not listed.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on fishtown.org or use the contact page to ask about the next general meeting
first_step.basis: The listing says all Fishtown residents and business owners are welcome, and meetings are open to the public; membership details are on the site but were not confirmed

records.notes: The website does not list the next meeting date. Monthly meeting format and the 3-meeting voting rule come from 2021 to 2022 reports and were not used as current facts. Email is behind the site's contact form, so no address is recorded. Mutual aid and zoning work on the site are in other families and are not described here.

records.name: Citizens Police Oversight Commission (CPOC)
records.summary: The city body that oversees Philadelphia police conduct. Its public meetings are open to residents, who can comment on agenda items.
records.notes: This is a city commission, not a joinable community group. Recorded so that the police_advisory interest has a reference point. The page lists a Zoom meeting on Oct 8, 2026, 6 to 7 pm; contact cpoc@phila.gov or 215-685-0891. Former Police Advisory Commission name.

notes: Budget: all 10 WebSearch calls used, 17 WebFetch calls used. The search results for this family were thin and mostly old (2011 to 2023). Four publish records came out (Block Captain Program, Germantown Jewish Centre TOCT, Fishtown Neighbors Association, and League of Women Voters of Philadelphia, which is low confidence because its own site was not found), plus one not_a_group (CPOC, a city commission). That is below the 20 to 40 target because the search budget ran out. Several guessed domains did not exist or were unrelated sites, so none were used. Strongest next steps: search for the Shissler, Fishtown Rec Center, and district-specific civic association pages by name; find the Philadelphia Town Watch program page; check the South Philly Action Coalition, Point Breeze Collective and Cedar Park Neighbors own sites from the Jan 2026 city guide. Not included: Student PIRGs New Voters Project postings on Idealist, which are paid jobs, not volunteer groups.
